* **Appl
ied or refused, never dropped.** A saved effort is applied by the route\n the run takes and recorded on the execution record, or

refused with
 `capability_missing` before any spend. An effort replaces the sampling
 temperature.
* **A selection belongs to
one model.** It must be for the `model` / `modelId` it\n sits beside (`400` otherwise); sent alone it pins its own model. A bare

model
 change on a suite or environment drops a selection saved for the old model
 instead of failing.
* **Cases keep their
selections.** A `models` PATCH replaces the array, but an\n entry that omits `selection` keeps the case's existing selection for
that\n model. Send `selection: null` to drop it.\n* **Clearing.** `null` clears a saved selection on a client `set`, an environme

nt
 or a suite, keeping the bare model id.
* **Never a secret.** A selection has no credential field; an unknown key
 (`apiKe
y`, …) is a `400`.\n* **Environments need the capability.** `GET .../environments/capabilities`\n reports `modelSelections`; an o
lder deployment rejects the field.\n* **`advancedConfig.reasoningEffort` is retired.** It was never applied, so\n writing it is a

`400` pointing at `models[].selection.settings`, and a stored
 value is refused by the runner.

`POST /chat-sessions/messages
` takes a top-level `reasoningEffort` for a\nper-request effort. Like `temperature`, it is pinned on the session's **first\nturn**
(a continuation that restates it is refused), it wins over the effort a\n`hostId`'s saved selection carries, and it cannot be com

bined with `temperature`.

The SDK, CLI, MCP tools and in-app agent all go through the same operations:
`--effort` / `reasoning
Effort` is a shorthand that edits the selection the target\nalready has, and is refused (`send modelSelection`) when there is none

.

## Not in the API yet

To set expectations while in preview, these are **not** available over the API
today (most exist in

the hosted inspector UI):

* Creating or revoking API keys (UI-only by design — see [Authentication](#authentication))
* Chat
and conformance suites\n* Browser-based OAuth flows initiated by the API (complete OAuth yourself,\n then upload the token to one

of the server's [accounts](#server-accounts))

If one of these blocks you, tell us on
[Discord](https://discord.gg/JEnDtz8X6z)

— it directly shapes what we
stabilize first.

## Versioning & stability

* The API is **path-versioned** (`/api/v1`). When
it reaches general\n availability, breaking changes will require a new version path.\n* **During the preview**, breaking changes
to v1 may still happen; we'll note\n them in the [changelog](https://docs.mcpjam.com/changelog/overview.md).\n* **Additive change
s** — new endpoints, new optional request fields, new\n response fields, new error codes — are considered non-breaking and can sh
ip\n at any time. Write clients that ignore unknown fields.\n* Error **codes** are stable identifiers; error **messages** are not

.

### Renamed surfaces

Three nouns this API used are now what the product calls them: `scenario` is
**study**, `journey` is
**goal**, and `wave` is **swarm run**. The paths, the\noperation names, the SDK types and the noun-bearing response fields all mo

ved:

| Was | Is |
| - | - |
| `/projects/{projectId}/scenarios[/{scenarioId}]` | `/projects/{projectId}/studies[/{studyId}]`
|\n| `/projects/{projectId}/user-testing/scenarios/{scenarioId}/…` | `/projects/{projectId}/studies/{studyId}/…` |\n| `/projects/{
projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/scenario` | `.../environments/{environmentId}/study` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/journeys[
/{journeyId}]` | `/projects/{projectId}/goals[/{goalId}]` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/journey-runs/{runId}` | `/projects/{projectI
d}/goal-runs/{runId}` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/journeys-overview`, `.../journey-findings` | `.../goals-overview`, `.../goal-fin

dings` |
| `/projects/{projectId}/waves/{waveId}/insights` | `/projects/{projectId}/swarm-runs/{swarmRunId}/insights` |

Respon
se fields followed their nouns: `scenarioId` → `studyId`, `journeyId` →\n`goalId`, `waveId` → `swarmRunId`, and `sessionsPerTarget

` → `iterations`.

Two reads became one: `get_scenario` served the execution settings and
`get_user_testing_scenario` served th
e environment id and the insights\nenvelope. `get_study` returns both, and the two caller-dependent fields are\nabsent rather than

null when you may not have them.

**Every old path still works** and is unchanged, including its old response
spellings. Each
one answers with `Deprecation: true` and a `Link` header naming\nits successor. They are undocumented on purpose — the spec is wha

t a new
integration reads — and they are removed at general availability.

A handful of operations kept their names through the
rename and so have no\ndeprecated twin to hold the old field spellings. `get_swarms_overview`,\n`create_swarm` and `update_swarm`

emit both and accept either — never both in
one request — until general availability.

### Vocabulary

A name can move behin
d an alias; a VALUE cannot. `sourceType` is one field with\none string in it, and a client switching on `\"scenario\"` has no seco

nd name to
fall back to. So the values negotiate.

Send `x-mcpjam-api-vocabulary: 2` and the renamed values read canonically:

| Field | Vocabulary 1 | Vocabulary 2 |
| - | - | - |
| session `sourceType` | `scenario` | `study` |
| session `parentRef.ki
nd` | `scenario`, `journeyRun` | `study`, `goalRun` |\n| session `parentRef` ids | `scenarioId`, `journeyRunId`, `journeyRefId` |
`studyId`, `goalRunId`, `goalRefId` |\n| share `resourceType` (field AND path segment) | `scenario` | `study` |\n| trace-destinati

on `sourceTypes` | `scenario` | `study` |

Absent means `1`, which is byte-for-byte today's contract. Any other value is a
`400
`. On the way IN, a vocabulary-2 request may name a filter or a path segment\nby either spelling; a vocabulary-1 request may use o
nly the legacy one, because\na boundary that accepts a spelling it does not announce is one two\nimplementations can disagree abou

t. A response that varies by vocabulary sends
`Vary: x-mcpjam-api-vocabulary`.

This is a **separate header** from `x-mcpjam-ev
al-vocabulary`, which is\neval-scoped by name and moves on its own schedule. A deployment may speak one\nand not the other, so rea
d\n`GET /projects/{projectId}/capabilities` — `apiVocabulary` and `vocabulary` are\ntwo blocks — before sending either. With the S

DK:
`new PlatformApiClient({ …, apiVocabulary: 2 })`, or
`client.withApiVocabulary(2)` on one you already hold.

Permalink res
ource types are the exception that proves the rule: `study` and\n`goal_run` are the canonical keys, `user_testing_scenario` and `j
ourney_run`\nstill resolve to the same routes, and which one a response carries follows the\nOPERATION rather than the header — a
renamed operation derives the canonical\nkey, its deprecated twin the old one. `capabilities.apiVocabulary.resourceTypes`\nlists b

oth.
